newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal PM threatens to quit after bill rejected.
newsitem.headline: Portugal PM threatens to quit after bill rejected.

text.p: Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Thursday that his government would resign if parliament gave final approval to a bill on local government financing that would jeopardise Portugal's entry to Europe's single currency.

"If a local financing bill receives final approval that leads to an increase in taxes and an aggravation of the public deficit, I shall no longer have the conditions to govern," Guterres said in an address to the nation broadcast on live television.

"The final approval by parliament of a bill that goes against our electoral promises, sacrificing the Portuguese to a brutal increase in taxes or an aggravation of the deficit, that would derail us from the path we have been taking in Europe, will lead immediately to my offer to resign," he added.
Earlier, opposition parties rejected a government bill on local government spending plans. In a parliamentary vote, opposition parties cast 109 votes to reject the bill against 102 in favour.

Guterres's Socialist government has said that opposition proposals for local government financing, which increase the funding received by local authorities, would boost overall public expenditure and lead to tax rises.
The government's bill proposes granting increased powers to local authorities, but does not increase their funding.

Guterres's government was elected in October 1995 after pledging to lead Portugal into the European single currency from the start in 1999 and promising not to raise taxes, but its victory fell four seats short of an absolute majority.

Guterres said in May that he wanted early elections if the main opposition parties pushed through parliament local government spending plans that would lead to tax rises and jeopardise Portugal's entry to the single currency.
Any decision to call early elections would be taken by President Jorge Sampaio.
